items.title: Ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang summoned to testify before Congress about affair with alleged Chinese spy
items.excerpt: Geopolitics/export controls: Congress formally summons Huang (and Commerce Secretary Lutnick) to testify over Nvidia chip flows to China via Megaspeed after his resignation.

items.title: US Congress eyes tighter curbs on chips to China
items.excerpt: US House Speaker Mike Johnson said on Thursday there was growing consensus in Congress on limiting chip exports to China after a spy scandal forced out Nvidia Corp CEO Jensen Huang (黃仁勳), who has pushed to preserve access to the Chinese market and has close ties with US President Donald Trump.Lawmak

items.title: Bessent puts Megaspeed heat on Lutnick: "Commerce has the pen"
items.excerpt: Treasury Secretary Bessent said Treasury, War, USTR and State had favoured putting Megaspeed on the entity list for months but 'Commerce has the pen' — the export-control decision on the alleged Nvidia AI-chip diversion channel sits with Lutnick's department.

items.title: 말레이, 앨리스 황 근무 메가스피드 자회사 AI반도체 유출 조사
items.excerpt: 말레이시아 투자통상산업부가 메가스피드 인터내셔널의 자회사 스피드매트릭스가 첨단 AI 반도체를 다른 국가로 유출했는지 공식 조사에 착수했다고 밝혔다.

items.title: Chinese AI labs are training models on Nvidia's Blackwell despite export controls, says ex-OpenAI engineer
items.excerpt: Former OpenAI engineer Will DePue published forensic evidence he says shows DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, MiniMax and Ant Group models were trained on export-restricted Nvidia Blackwell GPUs.

items.title: Nvidia privately confirmed it could track chips to fight smuggling, even as industry publicly questioned feasibility
items.excerpt: The Chip Security Act is getting renewed attention following Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation and reported affair with an alleged Chinese spy.

items.title: How Jensen Huang's exit from Nvidia impacts China's AI supply chain
items.excerpt: The founder’s stunning departure removes Beijing’s biggest advocate in Silicon Valley, accelerates chip stockpiling, and leaves Asian suppliers bracing for what comes next.

items.title: 젠슨 황 사임에 정부 긴급 점검…GPU 공급·협력 유지 총력(종합)
items.excerpt: 과기정통부가 엔비디아와 현안점검회의를 열어 첨단 GPU 26만장 공급과 협력 사업 지속을 재확인했고, 국가인공지능전략위원회는 긴급회의에서 국산 AI 반도체 활용 가능성을 검토했다.

items.title: EU leaders seek to tackle challenges in first AI summit
items.excerpt: EU leaders gathered in Dublin yesterday for their first ever summit on artificial intelligence (AI), to debate how the bloc can catch up with the US and China, and tackle funding issues and other problems.The meeting comes amid mounting worries about a technology that promises to transform industrie

items.title: EU deal on Ukraine talks overshadows AI-focused summit in Dublin
items.excerpt: The first informal European Council dedicated to AI met in Dublin on 13 November; leaders discussed AI sovereignty, compute and safeguards, but an agreement on Ukraine peace-talk representation dominated the outcome. Note: no adopted AI declaration text was found.

items.title: Court allows news publishers' copyright lawsuit against OpenAI to go ahead
items.excerpt: The Ontario Court of Appeal dismissed OpenAI's appeal of a jurisdiction ruling, letting Canadian news publishers' copyright suit over ChatGPT training proceed in Ontario rather than a U.S. court.
items.note: off-list exception: primary court ruling 11-13, no allowed-domain coverage found; thestar.com is a plaintiff — prefer the CP wire framing

items.title: Indonesia's new copyright bill would force Google and Meta to pay to aggregate news
items.excerpt: Meta, TikTok and Google testified in Indonesia's parliament against a copyright bill that would make platforms pay publishers for previews, including in AI search products, and when journalism is used to train AI models — which would make Indonesia the first Southeast Asian country to fold AI into copyright law.

items.title: Doctors want liability shield from AI mistakes
items.excerpt: The American Medical Association adopted policy calling for federal and state legislation shielding physicians from liability when AI products injure patients despite intended use, and for laws requiring AI vendors to carry liability insurance and disclose performance data.

items.title: 정부 "스마트안경 활용 부정행위 무관용…수능 철저 챙기겠다"
items.excerpt: 국무총리실은 13일 보도 설명자료에서 AI 스마트안경 등을 악용한 시험 부정행위에 무관용 대응하고, 수능 시험장별 판단 전담 인력을 배치하며 세무사 시험 의혹은 수사 의뢰하겠다고 밝혔다.

items.title: Whitehall to increase face-to-face job interviews after surge in AI applications
items.excerpt: In the most extreme cases, civil service leaders suspect that entire applications — including interviewees on a video calls — were generated by AI.

items.title: Jensen Huang's fall further exposes EU leaders on AI
items.excerpt: European leaders are meeting for their first conversation on AI with the tech world in tumult.

items.title: US public workers are fighting to protect their jobs from AI – and some are winning
items.excerpt: As governments adopt AI, workers are gaining ground in how it’s used and securing safeguards against its harms

items.title: Google faces calls for AI moratoriums in schools after Gemini pilot backlash
items.excerpt: Families confront Google after teen’s lawsuit labels Gemini a “suicide coach.”...

items.title: AI Kill Switches: What Policymakers Should Know
items.excerpt: Policymakers have recently proposed requiring “AI kill switches” to quickly stop an AI system or limit the impact of a harmful or unwanted AI incident. This piece describes different potential implementations of AI kill switches at each layer of the AI stack and offers key takeaways for policymakers.

items.title: Despite Huang Scandal, US-China AI Safety Dialogue Still Seems on Track
items.excerpt: Despite an inevitable increase in tensions in connection with the Huang affair, cooperation on AI safety appears to be on track, says Mark MacCarthy.

items.title: AI Is Killing Autonomously. Time for New Rules.
items.excerpt: The new reality urgently needs new rules that reach beyond individual human intent, writes León Castellanos-Jankiewicz.
